data.name: Faisalah
data.gender_notes: Faisalah is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who achieves, succeeds or manages to accomplish something, or the one who is entrusted with the responsibility of managing or succeeding to someone else in a position of power or authority. The name Faisalah carries the meaning “Successor, one who achieves” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Faisalah usually hope their child will grow to embody successor, one who achieves and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes achieving spiritual success and fulfilling one's purpose in life.
data.etymology: Faisalah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Successor, one who achieves.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Faisalah total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_english.long_meaning: Faisalah is derived from the Arabic root 'F-S-L', meaning to decide or judge. It signifies a final decision or judgement in a matter, often used in the context of Islamic law and judgement. The name holds significant spiritual and cultural importance across Muslim traditions.

data.cultural_impact: The name Faisalah is a name of Arabic origin, and is derived from the Arabic words 'Fa'il' (to do) and 'Salahah' (excellence, success, achievement), which translate to 'one who achieves, succeeds or accomplishes something'. historically, the name has been borne by numerous influential figures, both in Islam and beyond, including the first caliph of Islam, Abu Bakr, the second rightly guided caliph, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab and the eighth rightly guided caliph, Ali Zain al-Abidin. Hence, the name Faisalah is synonymous with leadership, power and success, and may be bestowed upon children as a source of pride and aspiration for achievement.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, the name Faisalah holds a deeper significance beyond worldly success and achievement. It is a reminder of the ultimate goal of life - to strive for the pleasure of Allah (swt) and to seek Allah's success and rewards in both this world and the Hereafter. As the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) said, "The whole life is a source of provision for the Hereafter, and the best types of provision are piety and knowledge." (Bukhari & Muslim) Thus, a person named Faisalah should continually strive to be a 'fa'il' (doer) of good deeds, and seek 'salahah' (excellence, success) not only in this world, but in the Hereafter by adhering to the teachings of Islam and living a God-conscious life (taqwa). May Allah grant us all the tawfiq (ability and success) to achieve the highest form of 'Faisalah' - gaining the pleasure of Allah (swt).
